translation_notes: prefixes: RDFS->rdfs, OWL->owl. RDF and XSD stay unused in the region's own body (they are only reached through context_shim's `_is_datatype`), so no @prefix rdf:/xsd: is declared -- an unused prefix would be noise.

the region's ONE navigation loop is a hand-written join wearing a `for` + early `continue`s: `for superclass in source_graph.objects(cls, RDFS.subClassOf)` narrowed by `(superclass, RDF.type, OWL.Restriction) not in source_graph` (an existence check). Both share the variable `superclass`, so they fuse into one `m{ {cls} rdfs:subClassOf ?superclass . ?superclass a owl:Restriction }` -- the stratum's headline gain. The following `source_graph.value(superclass, OWL.onProperty)` stays OUTSIDE the join, as `m{ {superclass} owl:onProperty ?v }.first()`: value() takes one onProperty, a joined motif would yield one solution per value.

the `isinstance(superclass, BNode)` check cannot move into the pattern (m{ } has no term-kind filter) and stays a Python guard, now applied per-solution after the Restriction check instead of before it -- a reordering of two pure, side-effect-free reads, so the observable result is identical (the driver's ex:Thing call has an owl:Restriction named by an IRI, which only this guard drops).

the eleven subsequent `source_graph.value(superclass, OWL.x)` single-value reads (exact/min/max/qualified/qualified-min/qualified-max cardinality, onClass, onDataRange, someValuesFrom, allValuesFrom) are each the textbook trav_single_value idiom and become `m{ {superclass} owl:x ?v }.first()` -- same construction the stratum table assigns to `g.value`, applied here inside a trav_navigation region because 'always the most specific construction' is per-idiom, not per-stratum.

fixture.ttl carries ten positive restrictions on ex:Widget (one per branch, including both arms of `_is_datatype`: the XSD-namespace check via someValuesFrom xsd:integer, and the rdfs:Datatype-declaration check via allValuesFrom ex:StatusEnum) and four negative neighbours that each satisfy exactly one or two of the three joined motifs but not all three -- proving the fusion actually joins. A second driver call on ex:Gadget (zero restrictions) exercises the empty-list zero-solution case.

`self` is a shared, stateless CardinalityConverter-shim instance reused for every call on both sides (see driver.py): a fresh instance per side would fail the harness's default `==` (object identity) for a reason with nothing to do with the translation.

Repair 2026-10-30: the translation fused owl:onProperty into the join, so a restriction carrying two owl:onProperty yielded two constraints where the original's `value()` yields one; proven by the driver's third call (ex:Thing, restriction t1: original pa only, translation pa and pb), fixed by reading onProperty with `.first()` outside a two-motif join.

repair.driver: third call on ex:Thing with eleven new fixture restrictions: two owl:onProperty on one restriction, an IRI-named owl:Restriction, an onProperty that is an owl:inverseOf blank node, owl:cardinality 0 alone, several someValuesFrom and onClass values, one neighbour per bound term of the restriction motifs (rdfs:seeAlso for subClassOf, rdfs:seeAlso owl:Restriction for rdf:type, owl:Class for owl:Restriction, rdfs:label for onProperty) and an owl:hasValue-only restriction
mutants_killed: owl:onProperty fused back into the join
repair.remaining: the join now covers two motifs instead of three: whether the pair stays directly-expressible and article_candidate is Maxime's call (triage question 1).

optimization_notes: Both sides: `min_count = max_count = int(x)` chained for the exact and qualified cardinalities; the three identical owl:onClass reads of the qualified branches become one read after them, applied when any of qual_card / qual_min / qual_max is set (same value each time, set before someValuesFrom and allValuesFrom can overwrite node_class, as in the original); the class-or-datatype typing of someValuesFrom and allValuesFrom becomes one loop over `(some_from, all_from)`, someValuesFrom keeping its own `min_count = 1`.

Exception to the symmetry rule, island only: optimized.ldpy joins the rdfs:subClassOf loop and the owl:Restriction existence test into one `m{ {cls} rdfs:subClassOf ?superclass . ?superclass a owl:Restriction }`, so the `if (superclass, RDF.type, OWL.Restriction) not in source_graph: continue` of optimized.py and its comment disappear; the BNode guard then follows the join (two pure reads reordered). The twelve `source_graph.value(superclass, OWL.x)` are `m{ {superclass} owl:x ?v }.first()` under one `@graph source_graph`.

Not compressed: owl:onProperty stays a `.first()` outside the join (a restriction with two owl:onProperty gives one constraint); the truthiness tests stay (`owl:cardinality 0` must add nothing); has_constraint stays a flag, since replacing it by one condition over eight values is longer and harder to read.
